title: From Minimum Wage Perth to Annual Salary: Tax, Super and the 38‑Hour Week
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38‑hour week. Includes tax, Medicare, super and the National Minimum Wage for Perth workers.
salarySummary: For a full‑time worker on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours a week, the annual gross pay is $52,257.44 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary in Australia?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full‑time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,257.44 per year. This is the gross annual amount before tax, Medicare, and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in Perth for 2026–27?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage applies across Australia, including Perth. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38‑hour week. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. Some awards or enterprise agreements may set higher rates.

faqs.q: How is tax and Medicare calculated on my annual pay?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The estimates here use the full tax‑free threshold and the 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds. No HELP, surcharge, or salary packaging is deducted.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: The Simple Formula

If you know your hourly rate and want to see what that means as an annual salary, the calculation is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This article assumes a standard full‑time week of 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. The result is your gross annual pay before tax, Medicare, and super.

For example, if you earn the **minimum wage perth** – which is the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour – your annual gross pay would be:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = **$52,257.44**

That’s the figure before any deductions. You can also work out your fortnightly pay: weekly pay × 2. At the minimum wage, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly is $2,009.80.

### What the Formula Does and Doesn’t Cover

This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It’s a starting point for comparing offers or understanding your baseline. For a more detailed breakdown, use [the timesheet](/), where you can enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. Many workers are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that pay more. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full‑time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week in May 2026 – well above the minimum.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the minimum wage, that’s $33.05 per hour. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** into the timesheet; instead, use the checkbox to add it automatically.

Superannuation Guarantee is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12%, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So on a $52,257.44 salary, your employer would contribute an extra $6,270.89 into your super fund. This is not part of your take‑home pay.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Pay

Once you have your gross annual figure, the next step is estimating tax and the Medicare levy. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: 45% on the excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The estimates here use the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a single person on the minimum wage ($52,257.44), the tax would be approximately $6,627 (using the 15% and 30% brackets) plus Medicare of $1,045.15, leaving a take‑home of around $44,585. See [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for more detail.

### Why the Figures Are Estimates

These calculations do not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. They also assume you are a resident for tax purposes and claim the full tax‑free threshold. Your actual pay may differ if you have deductions, offsets, or a different employment type. Always check with the Australian Taxation Office or a qualified adviser.

## Putting It All Together: A Perth Example

If you are earning the **minimum wage perth** – $26.44 per hour – your annual gross is $52,257.44. After tax and Medicare, you keep about $44,585. Your employer adds $6,270.89 to super. That’s a total employment cost of $58,528.33.

Compare that to the average full‑time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week ($108,352.40 per year). The minimum wage is about half the average. For award‑covered roles in Perth, rates may be higher – check the relevant [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) on this site.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

The [timesheet](/), our home page, lets you type your base hourly rate. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top. It converts to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, and shows estimated tax and super. Remember: the annual figure is hourly × hours per week × 52, assuming 38 hours. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly.

## Key Takeaways

- Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For full‑time, use 38 hours.
- The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week).
- Casual loading adds 25% on top; super is 12% paid on top of ordinary earnings.
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take‑home pay. Use the 2026–27 resident rates and 2% Medicare levy.
- The figures here are estimates. For your exact situation, consult [about the timesheet](/about) or speak to a professional.

Whether you are comparing a salary offer or checking your current rate, understanding the conversion from hourly to annual helps you make informed decisions. Start with the formula, then factor in tax, super, and any loadings or allowances.
